nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used an adversarial autoencoder (AAE) to learn the normative model. The AAE architecture included an encoder and decoder with two hidden layers each, and a discriminator. It was conditioned on demographic variables.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In this paper, we developed the normative model using the adversarial autoencoder (AAE)... In our analyses, we used a conditioned AAE.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Pinaya2021.pdf.md: Normative model / paragraph 1; Normative model training / paragraph 2

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical volumes for 68 cortical subregions and volumes of 33 neuroanatomical (subcortical) structures; volumes were normalized by total intracranial volume.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The final data included the cortical volume for each of the 68 cortical subregions (34 per hemisphere) and the volume of 33 neuroanatomical structures, totalling 101 subregions/ structures (the complete list is presented in the supplementary materials).; This involved estimating the relative brain region volumes for each subject by dividing the original brain region volumes by the total intracranial volume.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Pinaya2021.pdf.md: MRI processing.; Pinaya2021.pdf.md: Normative model training.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex used as conditioning variables in the autoencoder (one-hot encoded).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: This type of autoencoder allows us to influence the model's reconstruction using the demographic variables, i.e. age and sex.; To input these variables into the model, we transformed age and sex into one-hot encoding vectors.
